checks.message: Keep the name and the type: `L1.TendsToInfinity : (Nat → Nat) → Prop`.

hints.hint: Even the identity sequence fails. Read your quantifiers from left to right: can the threshold `N` depend on `M`? With `∃ N, ∀ M, …` it cannot.
`n / 2` is 0, 0, 1, 1, 2, 2, …. It tends to infinity, but it is not strictly increasing. Your definition should not require the sequence to increase.
This sequence goes up and down, and still tends to infinity. Monotonicity is not part of the notion.
Your definition accepts a constant sequence, so it is too weak. What must eventually happen for every bound `M`?
Your definition accepts a bounded sequence, so it is too weak. What must eventually happen for every bound `M`?
This sequence is unbounded but keeps falling back to 0. Being unbounded is not enough: from some index on, every term must be at least `M`.
A user of your definition needs this lemma. If it is ❓, the referee could not derive it from your definition: try a more standard formulation.
